Get started with zulake

Source: vignettes/zulake.Rmd
zulake.Rmd
library(zulake)

A Delta Lake table is a folder of Parquet files plus a log that says which files make up each version. Reading the files without the log returns deleted and superseded rows. zulake reads the log itself: this page opens a table, looks inside it, and then reads it.

Every section uses one table on Azure, and a function you supply that returns a bearer token:

uri <- "abfss://lake@account.dfs.core.windows.net/sales/orders"
token <- function() my_token()

Open a table

lake_open() builds a snapshot of one version, the latest unless you ask for another. A snapshot never changes; lake_load() gives you a new one.

tbl <- lake_open(uri, credentials = token)
lake_version(tbl)
lake_summary(tbl)
old <- lake_load(tbl, version = 3)

The log as data frames

Inspection is what zulake is for. Every action in the log comes back as a base data frame, unchanged, with nested values in list columns.

lake_history(tbl, limit = 10)
lake_schema(tbl)
lake_files(tbl)
lake_count(tbl)
lake_actions(tbl, version = lake_version(tbl))
lake_changes(tbl, from = 3)

Counts, sizes and statistics are 64-bit in the log. They come back as doubles, exact up to 2^53 - 1, and an error beyond; ask for int64 = "integer64" to get bit64 integers instead. A table whose files carry no statistics has an unknown row count: lake_count() says so with NA and a warning rather than counting only the files it can, and lake_count(tbl, footers = TRUE) reads those files’ counts from their Parquet footers.

Filters prune files, then rows

A filter is an R expression over column names. Partition values and statistics drop files that cannot match before anything is downloaded; the rows that remain are then filtered exactly, so the result never depends on the statistics. Local values are looked up where you call. Numbers in integer and decimal columns compare exactly, so a value a double cannot write exactly is given as text; strings compare in UTF-8 byte order.

lake_files(tbl, filter = year == 2026 & region %in% c("EU", "UK"))
yr <- 2026
lake_read(tbl, columns = c("id", "amount"), filter = year == yr & amount > "1000.10")

lake_walk() reads one file at a time and hands each piece to a function, for a table larger than memory. Columns qio cannot return yet (nested columns, decimals of more than 15 digits) are left out with a warning naming each.

total <- 0
lake_walk(tbl, function(piece) total <<- total + sum(piece$amount), filter = year == yr)

Unsupported features are refused

A table that needs a reader feature zulake does not support is refused with an error that names the feature, before any data is read, because ignoring it would return wrong rows. lake_protocol() shows which features a table uses, each marked supported; the error of a refused table carries the same data frame.

lake_protocol(tbl)
err <- tryCatch(
  lake_open("abfss://lake@account.dfs.core.windows.net/sales/widened", credentials = token),
  zulake_error_unsupported_feature = identity
)
err$feature
err$protocol
